entities.summary: Lê Thái Tông, birth name Lê Nguyên Long (黎元龍), was the second Emperor of the Lê dynasty of Đại Việt from 1433 until his death in 1442. Born on December 31, 1423, in Hanoi, he was the son of Lê Lợi, who had unified Đại Việt under the Lê dynasty. Lê Thái Tông's reign saw the expansion of the kingdom's borders, with the conquest of the neighboring Champa kingdom. He also oversaw the construction of several temples and monuments, including the iconic Temple of Literature in Hanoi. Despite his short reign, Lê Thái Tông's legacy continued to shape the politics and culture of Đại Việt for centuries to come. His successors would go on to build upon his achievements, creating a golden age of prosperity and cultural flourishing. As the Lê dynasty's second emperor, Lê Thái Tông's impact on Vietnamese history was significant, marking a new era of unity and growth under the dynasty's rule.
